lesson.title: Staff, Clefs and Note Names
lesson.summary: Five lines, two clefs and seven letters are enough to name any note.

section.title: The staff
section.p: Music is written on a staff: five horizontal lines with four spaces between them. Lines and spaces are counted from the bottom up.
A note sits either on a line, with the line through its middle, or in a space. The higher a note is written, the higher it sounds.

figure.staff: E4 F4 G4 A4 B4 C5 D5 E5 F5
figure.caption: Notes on every line and in every space of the staff, from the bottom up.

section.p: Notes are named with the first seven letters of the alphabet. After G the letters start again from A; the next note with the same letter is an octave higher.

section.title: Clefs
section.p: A clef at the start of the staff fixes which note belongs to which line. The two most common clefs are the treble clef and the bass clef.
The treble clef is also called the G clef: its curl wraps around the second line, which is G4, the G above middle C.

figure.caption: The treble clef marks G4 on the second line.

section.p: The bass clef is the F clef: its two dots sit on either side of the fourth line, which is F3, the F below middle C.

figure.caption: The bass clef marks F3 on the fourth line.

callout.p: Treble clef lines from the bottom: E G B D F. Spaces: F A C E.
Bass clef lines from the bottom: G B D F A. Spaces: A C E G.

section.title: Reading a note step by step

worked.title: Name the note on the fourth line of the treble staff

step.p: Start from the note the clef gives you: G4 on the second line.
Count up one letter for every line and every space: the second space is A4, the middle line B4, the third space C5.
The fourth line comes next, so the note is D5.

section.p: With practice you will recognise notes at a glance, but counting from the clef's note always works.

section.title: Ledger lines and middle C
section.p: Notes above or below the staff are written with short ledger lines, which extend the staff one line at a time.
Middle C, C4, lies between the two staves: on the first ledger line below the treble staff and on the first ledger line above the bass staff. Both notes below sound the same.

figure.caption: Middle C in the treble clef and in the bass clef.

check.prompt: Which note is on the middle line of the treble staff?

figure.description: Treble staff with one note on the middle line.

check.explanation: From G4 on the second line, the second space is A4 and the middle line is B4.

check.prompt: Which note is on the top line of the bass staff?
check.explanation: The bass clef marks F3 on the fourth line; the fourth space is G3 and the top line A3.

check.prompt: Where is middle C written in the bass clef?
check.option: On the first ledger line below the staff
On the first ledger line above the staff
In the top space of the staff
check.explanation: The top line of the bass staff is A3, the space above it B3, and the first ledger line above is C4.
